unboxing: Remove protective orange shipping locks from scanner and internal components
Connect power cable to main unit
Power on device using main power switch
initialSetup: Select language and region on touch screen
Set date, time, and time zone
Register device with Canon cloud services (optional)
Print configuration report to verify setup

ethernet: Connect CAT6 Ethernet cable to RJ-45 port on rear
On touch screen: Settings/Registration > Network > TCP/IP Settings
Choose Auto Obtain (DHCP) or configure Static IP
Print Network Status Report to verify
Access Remote UI at https://[printer-ip] (HTTPS recommended)
wifi: Requires optional Canon Wireless LAN Kit
Install wireless kit in designated slot
Power on device and navigate to Network Settings
Choose network SSID and enter WPA2/WPA3 password
Confirm connection and print network status
Note: Ethernet recommended for enterprise deployment

defaultCredentials.password: Must be set during initial setup - no default password

webInterface.certificateWarning: Canon imageRUNNER uses self-signed certificate by default. Browser will show security warning - this is expected. Upload CA-signed certificate via Remote UI for production use.
accessSteps: Print network status: Touch Menu > Output Reports > Network Status Report
Note IP address and HTTPS port (default: 8443)
Open browser to https://[printer-ip]:8443 OR http://[printer-ip] (redirects to HTTPS)
Accept certificate warning (click Advanced > Proceed or Add Exception)
Login with Administrator account and password set during initial setup
Remote UI dashboard loads with full device management capabilities
Access: Settings/Registration, Address Book, Job Log, Device Status, Security Settings

driverInstallation.windows10: Download Canon Generic Plus PCL6 driver or UFRII LT driver from usa.canon.com/support. For DX 4751i, select 'Generic Plus PCL6 V4 driver' for Windows 10. Run installer, choose 'Add Network Printer', select 'Search for Network Printers', choose device from list. For enterprise: Use Canon Universal Print Driver (UPD) for fleet deployment. Install via print server or push via GPO. Driver supports secure print, department ID, and account tracking.
driverInstallation.windows11: Same as Windows 10. Canon drivers fully support Windows 11 x64. Download Generic Plus PCL6 V4 or UFRII LT V4 from Canon support site. Windows 11 may auto-detect via WSD but full driver recommended for secure print, finishing options, and department ID. Canon recommends UFRII driver for best image quality and feature support.
driverInstallation.mac: Download Canon UFRII LT Printer Driver for macOS from usa.canon.com/support (version 10.19 or later for macOS 13+). Compatible with Apple Silicon. Run installer PKG file. Add printer via System Settings > Printers & Scanners > Add Printer. Select 'Canon DX 4751i' from list or enter IP manually. Choose 'Canon UFRII LT' driver when prompted. Supports AirPrint for basic printing without driver. Full feature requires Canon driver.
driverInstallation.linux: Download Canon UFR II Printer Driver for Linux from Canon support (RPM or DEB package). For Ubuntu/Debian: 'sudo dpkg -i cnrdrvcups-ufr2-*.deb'. For RHEL/CentOS: 'sudo rpm -ivh cnrdrvcups-ufr2-*.rpm'. Configure via CUPS at localhost:631. Select Canon imageRUNNER DX 4751i PPD file. Supports IPP and SMB printing protocols. Basic print and scan functionality. Advanced features (secure print, department ID) limited on Linux.

procedure: Access Remote UI at https://[printer-ip]:8443
Login as Administrator
Navigate to Settings/Registration (left sidebar)
Select 'Data Management' > 'Import/Export'
Choose 'Export Settings Data'
Select items to export: Network, Email, SMB, Department IDs, Address Book, Security
Check 'Include Encrypted Data' to backup passwords (recommended)
Click 'Start' to generate backup file
File downloads as .zip archive
Save securely with version/date: DX4751i_Backup_2024-11-16.zip
systemBackup.location: Downloads to local computer - store in secure backup location with restricted access

procedure: Access Remote UI and login as Administrator
Navigate to Settings/Registration > Data Management > Import/Export
Select 'Import Settings Data'
Click 'Choose File' and select previously saved .zip backup
Enter decryption password if backup was encrypted
Review items to be imported (Network, Email, Security, etc.)
Click 'Start Import'
Device processes import (may take 5-10 minutes for large configs)
Device will automatically restart after import completes
Verify all settings via configuration page after restart
prerequisites: Backup must be from same model series (imageRUNNER ADVANCE DX)
Firmware version should match or be newer than backup source
No active jobs should be running
Department IDs and user authentication settings will be restored
LDAP bindings may need reconfiguration depending on environment

procedure: Access Remote UI > Address Book Management
Select 'Export Address Book'
Choose export format: CSV (recommended) or LDIF
Select address book type: Local, Personal, LDAP
Choose which entries to export (All, Selected Groups, or Specific Contacts)
Click 'Export' to download file
Save as: DX4751i_AddressBook_2024-11-16.csv
Note: LDAP entries cannot be exported (configured separately)
Access Remote UI > Address Book Management
Select 'Import Address Book'
Click 'Choose File' and select CSV or LDIF file
Select import action: Add to existing OR Replace all
Map CSV columns to address book fields if needed
Review import preview
Click 'Start Import'
Verify imported contacts in address book
Test contact by creating scan destination using imported entry
prerequisites: CSV must have headers: Name, Email, Fax Number, SMB Path
Maximum 2000 entries in local address book
LDAP integration configured separately in Network Settings
Department ID restrictions apply if enabled

requirements: SMTP server address and port (25, 465, or 587)
SSL/TLS certificate if using secure SMTP (recommended)
smtpConfiguration: Access Remote UI > Settings/Registration > Send Settings
Enter SMTP Server Name: smtp.office365.com or smtp.gmail.com
Enter SMTP User Name (full email address)
Enter SMTP Password (use app password for Gmail)
Enable 'Use TLS' for secure connection (port 587 or 465)
Set maximum email size if needed (default 25MB)
Click 'OK' to save and test connection
authenticationSetup: Office 365: smtp.office365.com port 587, TLS required, use licensed mailbox credentials
Gmail: smtp.gmail.com port 587, enable 2FA and generate app password
Exchange on-premise: Internal server FQDN, port 25 or 587 depending on config
Ensure device IP is allowed in SMTP relay settings
Test relay: Remote UI > Send Settings > E-Mail/I-Fax > Send Test E-Mail
testProcedure: Remote UI > Settings/Registration > Send Settings > E-Mail/I-Fax
Review send log: Main Menu > Job Status > Communication Result
If failed, check error code in Communication Management Report
Common errors: #801 (Auth failed), #802 (Server connection failed), #805 (SMTP rejected)

requirements: SMB file share (Windows) or FTP server
Valid domain/local account with write permissions
SMB v2.0 or later recommended (v1.0 can be enabled if required)
smbConfiguration: Access Remote UI > Settings/Registration > Send Settings
Enter Display Name (shown on device panel)
Enter Host Name: Server FQDN or IP address
Select SMB Version: Auto-detect (or force v2/v3 for security)
Set File Format: PDF, JPEG, or TIFF (PDF recommended)
Configure file naming: Prefix, date/time stamp, counter
ftpConfiguration: Access Remote UI > Send Settings > File > FTP Server Settings
Enter Server Name: ftp.company.com or IP address
Enter User Name and Password for FTP account
Select Connection Mode: Passive (recommended) or Active
Choose File Format: PDF, TIFF, JPEG
authenticationSetup: Active Directory: Use DOMAIN\\username format (e.g., CONTOSO\\scanner)
Local Windows account: Use SERVERNAME\\username or WORKGROUP\\username
Verify account has write permissions to destination folder
Check both Share permissions AND NTFS security permissions
For security: Create dedicated service account for scanning
Test manually: Try creating file in destination using same credentials from another PC
Canon recommends SMB v2 or v3 (disable SMB v1 for security)
If using Department ID: Assign scan destinations to specific departments
testProcedure: In SMB/FTP Server Settings, select destination and click 'Connection Test'
If failed, check error: Authentication error, Path not found, Server unreachable
Perform test scan from device: Touch 'Send' > Select destination > Load document > Press Start
Check destination folder for scanned file
Verify file opens and contains expected content
Review send log: Main Menu > Job Status > Communication Result

requirements: USB flash drive or external HDD
Formatted as FAT32, exFAT, or NTFS
Front USB port (below control panel) or rear USB port
Note: USB scanning may need to be enabled by Administrator
procedure: Format USB drive as FAT32 for widest compatibility (exFAT for files >4GB)
Ensure USB scanning is enabled: Remote UI > Settings > Device Settings > Access Control > Enable USB Memory Media
Insert USB drive into front USB port (below touch panel)
Touch panel displays 'USB Memory Detected'
Touch 'Access Stored Files' or 'Save to USB'
Select 'Scan and Store' function
Choose scan settings: Color/B&W, Resolution (200-600 dpi), File Format (PDF/JPEG/TIFF)
Select Simplex (1-sided) or Duplex (2-sided)
Load document in ADF or place on platen glass
Press 'Start' to scan
Wait for 'Scan Complete' message
Safely remove USB: Touch 'Eject USB' before physically removing drive
Files saved with timestamp in /SCAN folder on USB
supportedFormats: Searchable PDF with OCR (requires OCR option)

configPages.meterPage: Touch screen: Main Menu > Counter > Print Counter List. Shows total impressions, copies, prints, scans, and consumable status.
configPages.configPage: Main Menu > Settings/Registration > Output Reports > Configuration Page. Prints complete device settings including network, security, and feature status.
configPages.networkConfigPage: Main Menu > Settings/Registration > Output Reports > Network Status Report. Shows IP, MAC, DNS, WINS, and all network protocol settings.
configPages.webInterface: Access Remote UI by entering device IP in web browser (https://192.168.1.100). Default admin login required. Configure HTTPS certificate for secure access. Remote UI provides complete device management, user administration, and fleet monitoring capabilities.

commonIssues: After initial setup, configure Scan and Send settings via Remote UI > Device Settings > Send
Set up LDAP integration for enterprise address book: Remote UI > Address Book Management
Configure department ID management for cost tracking if required
Enable audit logging for security compliance: Settings > Security Settings
For uniFLOW integration, install uniFLOW connector and configure authentication
Update firmware via Remote UI > Device Management > Firmware Update (requires Canon support account)

solutions: Power off device completely using main power switch
Wait 30 seconds
Power back on and allow full initialization
Check scanner cable connections
If error persists, contact Canon service - may require technician
Do not attempt to disassemble scanner unit

causes: Fixing unit at end of life
solutions: Power off device for 15 minutes to allow cooling
Power back on
Check fixing unit page count (replace at rated life)
Verify fixing unit is properly seated
Error may require Canon certified technician
Fixing unit replacement is covered under most service contracts
Follow on-screen instructions to locate jam
Open indicated cover and remove all jammed paper
Check paper quality and reload correctly
Ensure paper guides are properly adjusted
Clean feed rollers if jams are recurring
Replace pickup rollers if excessively worn

causes: Cartridge memory chip dirty or damaged
solutions: Remove toner cartridge
Clean cartridge memory contacts with dry lint-free cloth
Verify using genuine Canon GPR-57 toner
Reinstall cartridge ensuring it clicks into place
Close front cover firmly
If error persists, try different genuine Canon cartridge
Update firmware if using new toner batch

accessInstructions: Identify which drawer from touch screen display
Pull drawer completely out of device
Look for jammed paper at rear of drawer cavity
clearanceSteps: Remove all paper from drawer
Check for damaged sheets and discard
Remove any jammed paper from feed area
Check pickup roller condition
Reload paper ensuring stack is below max line
Adjust front and side guides to match paper size exactly
Reinsert drawer completely until it clicks
prevention: Use only paper within 52-300 g/m² specification
Fan paper before loading to prevent static
Do not mix different paper types in same drawer
Store paper in climate-controlled environment (20-25°C, 50-70% RH)
Replace pickup rollers at recommended intervals

accessInstructions: WARNING: Fixing unit is extremely hot - wait 30 minutes after power off
Open right door of main unit
Fixing unit is large assembly at rear
clearanceSteps: WAIT for fixing unit to cool completely
Pull green release lever on fixing unit
Gently remove jammed paper in direction of arrows
Do NOT touch fuser rollers - oils from skin cause print defects
Check for torn pieces and remove all paper fragments
Close right door firmly
Run test print to verify
prevention: Use correct paper weight setting in driver
Avoid printing on damp or curled paper
Replace fixing unit at rated life (300k pages for this model)
Keep fixing unit clean - schedule professional maintenance

accessInstructions: Open rear door (left side of device)
Locate duplex unit - blue lever visible
clearanceSteps: Pull blue lever to release duplex unit
Slide duplex unit out partially
Remove jammed paper carefully
Check duplex path for obstructions or torn pieces
Slide duplex unit back in until it locks
Close rear door
Run duplex test print
prevention: Use 60-120 g/m² paper for duplex printing
Avoid heavily textured or pre-punched paper for duplex
Clean duplex rollers during scheduled maintenance
Ensure paper is completely dry before loading

accessInstructions: Location indicated on touch screen display
clearanceSteps: Follow on-screen prompts for specific finisher jam location
Open indicated finisher cover
Remove jammed sheets
Check stapler unit for misfed staples
Close all finisher covers
Test stapling and finishing functions
prevention: Use only Canon-approved paper for stapling
Do not exceed stapling capacity (typically 50 sheets)
Replace staple cartridge before completely empty

solutions: Check toner level: Main Menu > Management > Consumables > Toner Status
Disable Toner Save: Settings > Preferences > Common Settings
Adjust print density: Settings > Adjustment/Maintenance > Image Quality Adjustment
Run gradation adjustment from touch screen
If drum is near rated life (80k pages), consider replacement
Shake toner cartridge gently and reinstall
Perform automatic image quality adjustment
Run drum cleaning cycle: Main Menu > Adjustment/Maintenance > Cleaning > Drum Cleaning
Clean scanner glass and platen with lint-free cloth and glass cleaner
Inspect drum unit for visible damage through front door
Print solid black test page to assess drum condition
Clean transfer roller if accessible
If drum is damaged, replacement required
Check for toner spillage inside device
Adjust image density lower: Settings > Image Quality > Density
Run special mode 3 adjustment for background removal
Ensure room humidity is 50-70% RH
Use higher quality paper (80 g/m² recommended)
Clean drum unit
Check transfer voltage settings (service mode)
If severe, may indicate drum or charging wire replacement needed
Check all paper cassette guides are snug against paper
Run paper transfer alignment: Main Menu > Adjustment/Maintenance > Adjust Image Position
Ensure paper is loaded straight in cassette
Clean registration rollers
Verify paper cassette is fully inserted
Check for foreign objects in paper path
Run automatic registration adjustment

diagnosticSteps: Print Network Status Report from touch screen
Verify IP address is valid and on correct subnet
Check Ethernet cable is securely connected
Test with different Ethernet cable and switch port
Verify network switch port is active and auto-negotiating correctly
solutions: If using DHCP, verify DHCP server has available addresses in pool
Assign static IP if DHCP is problematic
Check firewall rules aren't blocking device
Disable HTTP and enable HTTPS only for security
Update device firmware via USB if network update fails
Reset network settings to defaults: Network > Reset Network Settings
Configure DNS servers manually if auto-config fails
For enterprise networks, verify VLAN configuration matches policy

diagnosticSteps: Access Remote UI and navigate to Send Settings
Test SMTP server connectivity from another device
Review send logs in Remote UI > Log
solutions: Configure SMTP in Remote UI: Device Settings > Send > Email Settings
SMTP Server: smtp.office365.com or smtp.gmail.com
Port: 587 (STARTTLS) or 465 (SSL)
Enable SMTP authentication
Use app-specific password for Office 365/Gmail
Configure correct From address (must be valid email)
Test with internal SMTP server first
For Office 365, enable 'authenticated SMTP' in admin portal
Check firewall allows outbound SMTP traffic
For enterprise: integrate with Exchange server for authorized sending

diagnosticSteps: Test folder access from Windows PC with same credentials
Review security event logs on file server
solutions: Configure in Remote UI: Address Book > Register Destination
Use IP address instead of hostname: \\192.168.1.10\scans
Enter domain\username and password with Write access to share
Enable SMB2 or higher: Settings > Network > SMB Settings
On Windows server, enable SMB1 temporarily for testing (not recommended long-term)
Verify user has explicit write permissions to destination folder
Disable password-protected sharing on Windows for initial testing
For Active Directory environments, use domain credentials
Check Windows Firewall allows SMB traffic
Test with simple share first (e.g., \\server\test) before complex paths

symptoms: Canon PRINT app can't find device
diagnosticSteps: Verify device and mobile on same network/subnet
Check Bonjour/mDNS is enabled on network
Verify wireless is enabled if using Wi-Fi
solutions: Enable Apple AirPrint: Settings > Network > AirPrint Settings > Use AirPrint: On
Enable Mopria: Settings > Network > Mopria > Enable Mopria
Disable AP isolation on wireless router
Install Canon PRINT Business app (iOS/Android)
For Android: Use Canon Print Service plugin
Enable NFC for tap-and-print (requires optional NFC kit)
Update device firmware for latest mobile printing features
Check mobile device can ping printer IP address

procedure: Open front door of device
Grasp toner cartridge handle and pull straight out
Remove new GPR-57 cartridge from packaging
Rock cartridge gently 5-6 times to distribute toner evenly
Remove protective seal and tape
Insert cartridge until it clicks into place
Close front door - counter resets automatically

generalMaintenance.frequency: Every 80,000 pages or when 'Replace Drum' message appears
procedure: Order C-EXV51 drum unit in advance
Open front door and remove toner cartridge
Release drum unit lock lever (blue)
Pull drum unit straight out
Remove new drum from packaging - do NOT touch drum surface
Remove all protective covers from new drum
Insert new drum until it locks into place
Reinstall toner cartridge
Close front door
Reset drum counter: Main Menu > Adjustment/Maintenance > Reset Counter > Drum

generalMaintenance.frequency: Every 54,000 pages or when 'Replace Waste Toner Container' appears
procedure: Order WT-A3 waste toner container
Open front door
Locate waste toner container (right side, orange)
Pull container straight out - keep level to avoid spillage
Seal old container with cap (included with new container)
Insert new waste toner container until it clicks
Close front door - counter resets automatically
Dispose of old container per local e-waste regulations

generalMaintenance.frequency: Weekly for high-volume environments, monthly otherwise
procedure: Lift scanner unit / Platen cover
Spray glass cleaner on lint-free cloth (not directly on glass)
Wipe scanner glass, document glass, and white reference plate
Clean ADF feed rollers with damp cloth
Allow all surfaces to dry completely
Close scanner unit
Run test scan to verify no streaks
This is a comprehensive service performed by Canon certified technician
Includes replacement of: Fixing unit, transfer roller, pickup rollers, separation rollers
Full cleaning of all internal components
Lubrication of all mechanical assemblies
Firmware update to latest version
Comprehensive diagnostic tests
Calibration and adjustment procedures
Reset all maintenance counters
Typically covered under Canon service contract or can be purchased per-incident

generalMaintenance.frequency: Quarterly or as recommended by Canon
procedure: Check current firmware: Main Menu > Management > Device Information > Firmware Version
Login to Canon Partner Portal or contact Canon support
Download latest firmware file for imageRUNNER ADVANCE DX 4751i
Access Remote UI as administrator
Navigate to Device Management > Firmware Update
Upload firmware file (.BIN format)
Click Execute - device will show progress
Do NOT power off during update (typically takes 10-15 minutes)
Device will reboot automatically when complete
Verify new firmware version installed
Print configuration page to document update

generalMaintenance.task: Clean feed rollers and separation pads
generalMaintenance.frequency: Every 50,000 pages or when frequent jams occur
procedure: Power off device
Open all paper drawers
Locate pickup rollers at rear of each drawer opening
Dampen lint-free cloth with water (no chemicals)
Wipe rollers to remove paper dust and debris
Rotate rollers to clean entire surface
Clean separation pads in drawer
Allow to dry completely (15 minutes)
Reload paper and test feed from each drawer

firmware.updateProcedure: Access Remote UI > Device Management > Firmware Update. Upload firmware .BIN file from Canon Partner Portal. Requires administrator credentials.
